reason: Re-opened Rāmānuja through packet.js gita 12 --verse 12.5 (Govindacharya 1898, archive.org gita-bhasya). The evidence words stand verbatim in the 12.5 segment, where his comment on 12.3 to 12.5 is filed (packet note confirms the grouping): 'Avyakta-Path is the getting the mind to think of the subject relating to avyakta=Individual soul. This is attained with great struggle by the emodted i.e., those who love the body as if it were the atma'. The same comment glosses akshara as 'individual soul-nature' and his rendering of 12.5 has 'indiscernible (atma)', so reading the Unmanifested as the individual soul is his (pratyagātman), not Besant's or the proposer's; 'those who love the body as the self' and 'great struggle' are in his words; 'think on only with great struggle' is a fair compression of 'the getting the mind to think ... attained with great struggle', no drift. Locator 'on 12.5' right. Plain sense matches 12.2 to 12.4 (best in yoga; 'these also come unto Me'), no four-word run from the key, no doctrine; its one soft spot is 'the Imperishable', which is Telang's and the commentators' word, where Besant's text says 'the Indestructible' (12.1, 12.3): same referent, not a false claim. School named. No comparison, not a hard passage. verse.js ok (ref Bhagavad Gita 12.5, at [473]); entry-check.js ok, no errors or warns; 43 words, one semicolon, one full stop, no dash. Key verse agrees in sense with Telang ('the unperceived goal is obtained by embodied beings with difficulty').
better: Optionally use Besant's own word in the plain sense: 'though worshippers of the Indestructible reach him too'.
